name: Daman-Diu Portuguese
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant, final' (final stress) rests on Cardoso's APiCS sketch sentence, which I confirmed verbatim in the downloaded survey page. The author's full reference grammar (Cardoso 2009, LOT 210, 335 pp.), downloaded now, states the same rule at length (section 5.4, p. 100: stress predictably on the final syllable, phonologically assigned, with phonetic/phonological/morphological/etymological arguments and stress shifting onto suffixes), with only unadapted English loans as exceptions, so 'dominant not strict' is right. Dalgado 1903 independently reports that Daman creole reduces paroxytones and proparoxytones to oxytones, so the Daman half of the languoid agrees. No instrumental study was found. Action: fill the empty quote/cite/loc/grade fields with Cardoso 2009 section 5.4 p. 100 as the primary citation (APiCS ch. 39 as secondary) and upgrade the strength of the evidence; no recod

sources.citation: Cardoso, Hugo C. 2009. The Indo-Portuguese language of Diu. (LOT Dissertation Series 210.) Utrecht: LOT. xii+335 pp. PhD dissertation, Universiteit van Amsterdam.
sources.quote: "DIP is a stress-accent language ... Stress falls predictably on the word's final syllable, and as such can be said to be phonologically assigned rather than morphologically determined." Evidence: final syllables most prominent in pitch and usually intensity; mid-vowel height contrasts only in final syllables; stress moves onto verbal suffixes (/fal/ 'speak(s)' vs /fa.'lo/ 'spoke'; /a.'paj/ vs /a.p@.'No/); Portuguese post-tonic syllables dropped (/ku.'bErt/ 'blanket', /muz/ 'music'). Fn. 15: 'stress always falls on the last syllable'. Exceptions: unadapted Indian-English borrowings (jungle, li

sources.citation: Cardoso, Hugo. 2013. Diu Indo-Portuguese. In Michaelis, Maurer, Haspelmath & Huber (eds.), The survey of pidgin and creole languages, vol. 2, 90-101. Oxford: OUP. Online version: APiCS Online survey chapter 39, apics-online.info/surveys/39.
sources.quote: "Stress falls predictably on the word’s last syllable." Also: close-mid/open-mid contrast only in stressed position; medial syllable of trisyllables weakly prominent with /ə/ often deleted.

sources.citation: Dalgado, Sebastião Rodolfo. 1903. Dialecto indo-português de Damão. Lisboa (offprint from Ta-Ssi-Yang-Kuo). archive.org id dialectoindopor01dalggoog (scanned text).
sources.quote: "Não ha esdrúxulos nos crioulos norteiros ... no de Damão reduzem-se, bem como os paroxytonos, a oxytonos: bufl < búfalo, arvr < árvore, famil < família, ... vigar < vigário" (no proparoxytones in the northern creoles; in Daman both proparoxytones and paroxytones are reduced to oxytones). Also notes accent displacement maná < mana, sinhorá < senhora in verse. Bears on the Daman half of the dama1278 languoid, which the APiCS/Cardoso sources do not cover: consistent with final stress.
sources.locator: phonology section, heading 'Esdrúxulos', c. pp. 7-8 of the offprint (djvu the text)

tone.quote: A posição pós-túnica não é relevante para o estudo em questão, uma vez que qualquer sílaba pós-tónica nos étimos portugueses não foi retida no crioulo indo-português de Diu. [scanned of the scan; 'pós-túnica' is the scanned rendering of printed 'pós-tónica'] ... No crioulo de Diu, tal como sucedia no português clássico, a presença de uma vogal alta na sílaba tónica pode motivar a elevação da vogal átona; ex.: /bonit/ 'bonito, bom': [bun'i] / [bo'nit] ... O crioulo de Diu não acompanhou este processo diacrónico; como tal, ao português moderno pegar [pa'gar] contrapõe-se em crioulo pega [pe'ga]; ao português moderno mostrar corresponde em crioulo mestra [mos'tra].
tone.locator: footnote 3 on p. 112 (sec. 3.1 'O sistema vocalico') for the post-tonic sentence; the /bonit/ vowel-raising example and the pegar~pega [pe'ga], mostrar~mestra [mos'tra] contrast are both on p. 114 (before the '114 |' footer), not pp. 113-114; no tone/intonation passage anywhere in pp. 107-117
tone.translation: Post-tonic position is not relevant to the present study, since no post-tonic syllable of the Portuguese etyma was retained in the Indo-Portuguese creole of Diu. ... In the Diu creole, as in Classical Portuguese, the presence of a high vowel in the tonic (stressed) syllable can trigger raising of the unstressed vowel; e.g. /bonit/ 'pretty, good': [bun'i] / [bo'nit] ... The Diu creole did not follow this diachronic process; thus modern Portuguese pegar [pa'gar] contrasts with creole pega [pe'ga]; modern Portuguese mostrar corresponds to creole mestra [mos'tra].
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
